subject: Cost benchmarking: $/1M targets vs OpenAI/Anthropic & next steps
messages:
From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@averyhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@averyhealth.com>, procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-28T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up questions on cost

Thanks for the demo today, Camila — liked the low-latency routing for clinical prompts. Two quick items on costs that came up internally:

- We need a target unit we can budget to: finance asked for a $/1M tokens target for planning. Can you provide a baseline and high/low scenarios?
- How do you position vs OpenAI and Anthropic on a per-1M basis for comparable quality profiles? We run mostly 2k-context chat with a good amount of embeddings for search; totals estimated 100M–300M tokens/month in year one.

Also looping procurement to start a draft SOW. Appreciate a concise comparison and a recommended target to take to finance.

—Dana
Senior Product Manager, Avery Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@averyhealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-28T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up questions on cost

Dana — great questions. Per our internal notes during the call, I ran a quick pass on target $/1M buckets and attached a spreadsheet with scenario rows (unit-rate-scenarios.xlsx) and a draft mutual action plan. High-level summary below.

Baseline assumptions (please confirm):
- Workload mix: 60% chat (avg 2k context), 30% embeddings, 10% rerank/batch.
- Expected volume year1: 100M–300M tokens/month (you mentioned that range).
- Target SLOs: 100–200ms p50 for short prompts, burstable peak throughput for batch embeddings.

Benchmark snapshot (comparable quality / production features):
- OpenAI (default highest-cap): ~ $X per 1M tokens (host-managed throughput, variable burst costs)
- Anthropic: ~ $Y per 1M tokens (similar pricing band depending on model family)
- Public-hosted open-models (Replicate/Other hosts): wide variance ($Z–$W per 1M)

Redwood positioning (what we can offer):
- Target commercial ask: $/1M tokens in the $A–$B range depending on commit and routing (dedicated vs hosted) — see spreadsheet tiers.
- Committed Dedicated option (12mo): lower $/1M, fixed throughput and SLA.
- Hosted API option: faster time-to-value, slightly higher $/1M for burstable scenarios.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the mix (chat vs embed vs batch) and pick a mid-point volume (e.g., 200M/mo) so we can model unit economics.
2) I’ll produce a two-line commercial: (a) 12-mo committed Dedicated with $/1M tiers, (b) Hosted pilot with a pilot credit and per-1M pricing for evaluation. Both will include a migration path to Private if needed.
3) Procurement: share the SOW draft; we’ll add standard SOC2 clause and a 30-60 day data export SLA.

Attached: unit-rate-scenarios.xlsx (scenarios tab highlights $/1M targets across commit levels) and draft SOW stub (Avery_MA_Draft.pdf).

Will send a short comparative price table in a follow-up email (wanted to validate your volume mix first). If OK, I’ll include Ben on the commercial terms.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: unit-rate-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), Avery_MA_Draft.pdf (SOW stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir@averyhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@averyhealth.com>, procurement@averyhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up questions on cost

Camila — thanks. Quick clarifications from finance:
- Our finance team wants a conservative and an optimistic $/1M number for modeling. Conservative = worst-case (hosted/no-commit), optimistic = committed 12–24mo.
- Are there predictable volume breakpoints (e.g., discounts at 100M, 200M, 500M) we should model?

Also, is there an easy way to compare the tokenization differences: our prompt sizes are variable; do you model tokens the same way OpenAI reports them? That impacts the $/1M equivalence.

—Samir
Director of Finance, Avery Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@averyhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.lee@averyhealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up questions on cost

Samir — quick notes from pricing ops:

1) Conservative vs optimistic model
- Conservative (hosted, no-commit): assume a premium + overhead for caching/multi-tenant. Rough benchmark: OpenAI-like host equivalent = $~30–40 per 1M tokens for the high-cap models we compared (this is a modeled, not list price; exact depends on model family).
- Optimistic (12–24mo commit, Dedicated): we can drive $/1M into the low-double-digits at scale (examples: $10–18/1M depending on volume and whether embeddings-heavy workloads allow more aggressive batching).

2) Volume breakpoints we typically model
- Tier1: <100M/mo — limited discount
- Tier2: 100–300M/mo — meaningful step down (commit required for lowest bands)
- Tier3: 300–1B/mo — top-tier economics, custom capacity planning

3) Tokenization parity
- We normalize tokens using the open-source tiktoken-compatible tokenizer we use in our evals. For commercial comparisons we publish an equivalence table in the spreadsheet (sheet: token-parity).

Next actions from our side:
- Camila to send the priced two-line (hosted pilot vs dedicated commit) and populate the conservative/optimistic $/1M numbers in the spreadsheet.
- Samir / Avery to confirm the volume mid-point (recommended: 200M/mo) and sign off on a pilot scope.

I’ll also flag ops to estimate ingress/egress and embedding batch-run discounts for the committed proposal.

—Ben
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: unit-rate-scenarios.xlsx
